title: Cold tea
label: YOUR TEA IS GETTING COLD
lead: Hook 1 (The object truth), because the contrast between phone and tea lands in the first sentence and the kit draws those two objects best.

hooks.label: YOUR TEA IS GETTING COLD
hooks.say: Your phone gets your full attention. Your *tea* just gets cold.

hooks.label: FIRST SIP HOT. NEXT SIP COLD.
hooks.say: You make tea, sit down, open your phone, and the next sip is *cold*.

hooks.label: WHEN DID YOU FINISH IT HOT?
hooks.say: When did you last finish a cup of tea while it was still *hot*?

beats.say: Your phone gets your full attention. Your *tea* just gets cold.
beats.scene: Top-down on a dark table: a steaming mug above a bright, buzzing phone. On 'cold' the steam thins out.

beats.say: You made it properly, the good mug, just the right *sugar*.
beats.scene: Warm morning light, low angle on the mug. Thick steam. A sugar cube drops in on 'sugar'.

beats.say: Then one quick look becomes a long scroll through other people's *lives*.
beats.scene: A dark room. A phone stands upright on the table, its feed scrolling faster and faster, its glow the only light.

beats.say: The steam gets thinner and you never even see it *go*.
beats.scene: Close on the mug. The last wisps of steam fade and the light cools from amber to blue on 'go'.

beats.say: So turn the phone face down and drink it while it's *warm*.
beats.scene: The phone flips face down and its glow dies. The room warms up and steam rises again on 'warm'.

beats.say: Hot tea waits for nobody. Most good moments don't either.
beats.scene: Wide and quiet: the mug alone on the table in a pool of warm light, steam curling, a sign on the wall reads DRINK IT HOT.
